target.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After upgrading an install that stored credentials in per-agent `auth-profiles.json` to a 6.x build, **every agent fails with `401 invalid api key`** for any provider whose credentials resolve through an auth profile.

The runtime auth-profile store now loads exclusively from the per-agent SQLite store (`auth_profile_store` in `<agentDir>/openclaw-agent.sqlite`). The legacy `auth-profiles.json` → SQLite import only runs through `openclaw doctor --fix`, behind an interactive prompt. So after a normal upgrade the SQLite store is empty:

- `openclaw models auth list --agent <id>` → `Profiles: (none)`
- `resolveAuthProfileOrder` returns `[]` (empty `store.profiles` → empty `storeProfiles` → empty `baseOrder`)
- the provider can't resolve its referenced profile → `401 invalid api key` on every agent

The credentials in `auth-profiles.json` are still valid — they are just never read at boot.

## Root cause

`loadAuthProfileStoreForAgent` (`src/agents/auth-profiles/store.ts`) already back-fills the legacy `oauth.json` into an empty SQLite store via `mergeOAuthFileIntoStore`, but there is **no equivalent back-fill for `auth-profiles.json`** (the flat api_key/token profiles). They only get imported by the `doctor --fix` migration.

## Fix

Mirror the existing oauth back-fill: add `mergeLegacyJsonProfilesIntoStore(store, agentDir)` (`persisted.ts`) and call it alongside `mergeOAuthFileIntoStore` when the SQLite store is empty, persisting the result one-shot.

The comprehensive `doctor --fix` migration (backup + delete the JSON + AWS-SDK markers + OAuth sidecar handling) is unchanged; this only adds a lazy safety-net for the common api_key/token case and does **not** delete the JSON.

## Reproduction

Minimal (added as a test): an agent dir with an `auth-profiles.json` api_key profile + empty SQLite store → `loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntime(agentDir).profiles` is empty before the fix, and contains the profile (persisted to SQLite) after.

Real: upgraded a production install (9 agents) from `2026.5.28` to `2026.6.6`. Every agent returned `All models failed: ... 401 invalid api key`; `auth_profile_store` had 0 rows; `paste-api-key` / `doctor --fix` populated SQLite and restored auth (survives restart).

## Testing

- New test in `profiles.test.ts` (`legacy auth-profiles.json lazy migration`): passes with the fix, fails without it.
- `tsc` typecheck and `oxlint` clean on the changed files.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Evidence

Run locally against this branch (post-push head), Node 24 / pnpm 11, vitest 4.1.7. The auth-profiles tests run under `test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts` (the unit config excludes `src/agents/**`).

### Validation (re-runnable)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts -t "legacy auth-profiles.json lazy migration"
#  Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 2 passed | 11 skipped (13)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts
#  Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 13 passed (13)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts "src/agents/auth-profiles/"
#  Test Files 20 passed (20)   Tests 241 passed (241)
```

### Before/after behavior (not source inspection)

A harness seeds a per-agent legacy `auth-profiles.json` (`{ "litellm:manual": { type:"api_key", provider:"litellm", key:"…" } }`) plus an **empty** SQLite store, then calls the real `loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntime(agentDir)` and `resolveAuthProfileOrder({ store, provider:"litellm" })` (no `cfg`, so any candidate comes purely from the store back-fill). Run unchanged against both commits:

**BEFORE** (parent commit, fix absent): `resolveAuthProfileOrder` returns no candidates → auth would 401; SQLite is never created.
```json
{ "resolveAuthProfileOrder_litellm": [], "sqlite_exists_after_load": false }
# AssertionError: expected [] to include 'litellm:manual'
```
**AFTER** (this branch): the legacy profile is imported on load, resolves, and is persisted (survives JSON deletion).
```json
{ "runtime_litellm_manual": { "type":"api_key", "provider":"litellm", "key":"legacy-secret-key" },
  "resolveAuthProfileOrder_litellm": ["litellm:manual"],
  "loadPersisted_post_load_keys": ["litellm:manual"], "sqlite_exists_after_load": true }
```
Only the commit differed; harness and seeded inputs were byte-identical.

### oauthRef-only profiles are skipped

`mergeLegacyJsonProfilesIntoStore` reuses the store's canonical `evaluateStoredCredentialEligibility` (the same gate `resolveAuthProfileOrder`/doctor use) and skips entries whose `reasonCode === "unresolved_ref"` — the OAuth sidecar shape doctor deliberately leaves in JSON until token material exists. New test: a legacy JSON with an `api_key` profile **and** an `oauthRef`-only `openai-codex:default` → after load, SQLite contains `litellm:manual` only; `openai-codex:default` stays in JSON (undefined in store). Negative control: temporarily disabling the skip makes that test fail (`expected { type:'oauth', … } to be undefined`), confirming the guard is genuinely exercised.

### Why steady-state loads stay safe

The import only fills profile ids **absent** from SQLite (`if (store.profiles[profileId]) continue;`), so it is **idempotent** — once a profile is back-filled and persisted, later loads short-circuit and never re-read or overwrite it. With the eligibility gate it now promotes only resolvable credentials, matching doctor's boundary. Net: upgraded installs recover working auth on the first load without a doctor round-trip, while the SQLite-only steady state is preserved as soon as the one-time back-fill completes.

Files: `src/agents/auth-profiles/persisted.ts` (`mergeLegacyJsonProfilesIntoStore`, skip via `credential-state.ts`), `store.ts` (`loadAuthProfileStoreForAgent`), `order.ts` (`resolveAuthProfileOrder`), test in `profiles.test.ts`.

target.title: fix(msteams): sanitize internal tool-trace lines from outbound text (#90684)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MS Teams sends assistant text to users **without** running `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()`, so internal tool-trace lines leak into user-visible messages. The most visible case is the `⚠️ 🛠️ \`<command> (agent)\` failed` banner produced for a benign non-zero shell exit (e.g. a `grep` that finds no match → exit 1). The turn completes successfully, but the user receives an alarming "failed" message from the bot.

`msteamsChannelOutbound` had no `sanitizeText` hook at all. This is the MS Teams instance of #90684. Discord, Google Chat (#95084, merged) and WhatsApp already run the canonical sanitizer on outbound; MS Teams was missing it.

Closes part of #90684. Related: #88332, #95084 (the merged Google Chat counterpart, identical fix shape).

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` to `msteamsChannelOutbound`, reusing the canonical delivery sanitizer the other channels already use (rather than new regexes). The hook runs in the shared outbound deliver path, so it covers every text send — replies, sub-agent announces, and cron deliveries. `msteamsChannelOutbound` is now exported so the hook can be unit-tested (mirrors `googlechatOutboundAdapter`).

Out of scope: the Codex-native warning taxonomy (#88332) and threading/attachments. This is one focused MS Teams instance of the cross-channel umbrella.

## User Impact

Internal trace/failure banners (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ … (agent) failed` from a benign `grep` no-match) are no longer shown to MS Teams users. Legitimate assistant prose is unaffected. No config, auth, secrets, network, or tool-execution behavior changes.

## Evidence

The fix wires the canonical `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` into the MS Teams outbound `sanitizeText` hook. Below is copied live output / console output (stdout) from running that exact function via `node` on a live OpenClaw `2026.6.8` deployment, with the leaked banner as input:

```
IN : "Listo, ya lo cargué.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E (PV-123) /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed"
OUT: "Listo, ya lo cargué."
```

The banner line is removed; the real assistant prose is preserved.

A new unit test exercises the actual patched adapter hook:
`pnpm vitest run extensions/msteams/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts -t "sanitizeText"` → **2 passed** (`msteams outbound sanitizeText`): asserts `msteamsChannelOutbound.sanitizeText` strips the `(agent) failed` banner and leaves ordinary prose untouched.

**Proof limitations:** the MS Teams deployment available to me runs `2026.5.28`, which predates the banner machinery (it does not generate the `(agent) failed` banner — `(agent)`/`🛠️` are absent from its payload builder), so it cannot reproduce the end-to-end leak. The after-fix evidence therefore exercises the exact canonical sanitizer this PR wires into MS Teams, captured on a live `2026.6.8` deployment, plus the adapter-hook unit test. No MS Teams client screenshot; private space/account/user details omitted.

## Risk

Highest-risk area is over-stripping legitimate content. Mitigated by reusing the canonical `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` (already shipping for Discord/Google Chat/WhatsApp) rather than new logic, plus the new unit test asserting ordinary prose is preserved.

AI-assisted change.



---

## Real behavior proof

Local run against this branch, pnpm 11.2.2 (frozen lockfile), vitest.

### Validation (re-runnable)

```
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts -t "sanitizeText"
#  Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 2 passed | 2 skipped (4)
# full file: Tests 4 passed (4)
```

### Before/after (patched MS Teams outbound path)

Input (identical both runs):
```
Here is your summary.
⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E 'PV-123' /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed
The report is ready.
```
A repro drives the real `deliver.ts` sanitize gate; BEFORE = adapter `sanitizeText` undefined (main), AFTER = the patched `msteamsChannelOutbound.sanitizeText` export.
```
[BEFORE main]  OUT: "Here is your summary.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `grep -E 'PV-123' /tmp/out.txt (agent)` failed\nThe report is ready."
[AFTER patch]  OUT: "Here is your summary.\nThe report is ready."
```
BEFORE: the `⚠️ 🛠️ … (agent) failed` banner survives into outbound text. AFTER: the banner line is removed, both prose lines preserved.

### Why main leaks

`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts` applies `handler.sanitizeText` only when present (`:795`). On main `msteamsChannelOutbound` has no `sanitizeText`, so the shared gate is skipped and text passes through verbatim. This PR adds `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` at `extensions/msteams/src/channel.ts:444`, mirroring the merged Google Chat fix #95084. Canonical sanitizer: `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts` → `stripAssistantInternalTraceLines()`.

**Proof limitation** (consistent with the PR's existing note): the AFTER side exercises the hook through a faithful re-implementation of the `deliver.ts` gate (the real gate is module-internal, not exported), not a live MS Teams socket send.

target.title: fix(msteams): bound probe token acquisition to request deadline
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready, no follow-up required
- Squashes cleanly onto `a788617325` (origin/main) — no rebase needed
- All sibling MS Teams call sites already use `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`; this PR brings the probe in line with the established pattern
- No new public API, no SDK surface change, no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "network layer bound" wave
- The test rewrite addresses the ClawSweeper P2 (automation) finding by replacing wall-clock waits with `vi.useFakeTimers()`. The scratchpad harness in section 4.2 addresses the P1 (needs proof) finding by exercising the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` + `@azure/msal-node` path against a stalled loopback `node:http` server.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`probeMSTeams()` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89` awaits `tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` for the Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph token endpoints with no surrounding deadline. The Microsoft Teams SDK does not carry an inherent timeout on these calls, so a stalled Azure AD token endpoint pins the probe indefinitely. Six other MS Teams paths already wrap the same SDK calls with `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` (default `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`); the probe was the one missing site.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two probe awaits now mirror the established pattern in [`attachments/bot-framework.ts:252-256`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.ts) and [`attachments/graph.ts:258-262`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.ts) — wrap the SDK call in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` with a descriptive `label`. The default 30s bound is identical to the bound the sibling paths use. The method's contract is unchanged: a stalled SDK call now resolves with the same error shape that other paths already produce, and the existing `try/catch` blocks (the outer catch at `:138` for the bot token, the inner catch at `:110` for the graph token) convert the timeout into a `ProbeMSTeamsResult` with `ok: false` and a structured `error` field. No new helper is introduced; the fix reuses the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API or SDK surface.

## User Impact

Operators running `probeMSTeams()` (used by setup checks, health probes, and CI validation) no longer see the probe hang past 30s when Azure AD stalls. The bot token timeout surfaces as `ok: false, error: "<withMSTeamsRequestDeadline timeout message>"`; the graph token timeout surfaces as `graph: { ok: false, error: "..." }` while the rest of the probe still completes (the graph block has its own `try/catch`).

## Evidence

### 4.1 Focused vitest output — fake-timer rewrite

The committed regression guard at [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts) drives the **real** `probeMSTeams()` code path under `vi.useFakeTimers()` so the 30-second production deadline from `withTimeout` (`@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/timing.js:25`, uses `setTimeout`) resolves in milliseconds instead of waiting 30 wall-clock seconds per case. The wrapper behavior is asserted without paying deterministic CI cost.

Command:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Result (5 cases, focused wall-clock 15.23s — transform + import only; tests themselves total 39ms):

```
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the bot token stalls 25ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the graph token stalls 3ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when both tokens stall 2ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns ok=true for a normal (non-stalled) probe 1ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > uses the documented 30s production default deadline for both token acquisitions 2ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
   Start at  23:43:12
   Duration  15.23s (transform 8.40s, setup 557ms, import 14.38s, tests 39ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 21.72s
```

Per-case wall-clock after the first version of this PR: 90s of stalled-wait (`Promise.race` against a real `setTimeout` budget). After the rewrite: 25ms / 3ms / 2ms / 1ms / 2ms. The fifth case asserts the production default deadline is exactly `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` by spying on `withTimeout`'s `timeoutMs` argument, so the production contract is not silently weakened by the fake-timer change.

### 4.2 Exact-head controlled MS Teams SDK transport proof

The P1 (real-SDK proof) finding is addressed by a temporary uncommitted harness that drives the production `probeMSTeams` entry point through the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` constructor and real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication.acquireTokenByClientCredential`. MSAL's outbound `fetch` calls (the OIDC discovery GET and the token POST to `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/...`) are redirected via a `globalThis.fetch` monkey-patch to a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that selectively stalls. No mocked fetch adapter; no real Azure traffic; no credentials.

- Exact head: `082f48e96c04f9680b46029a392ac83d8264c1d2`
- Scope: production `probeMSTeams()` wrapper path → production `loadMSTeamsSdkWithAuth()` → real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` (token manager) → real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication` → `globalThis.fetch` (patched) → loopback `node:http` server. The wrapper `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` is the real production helper; the SDK, MSAL, and HttpClient are unmodified real packages.

Redacted command form actually run:

```bash
PROOF_HEAD=082f48e96c \
  HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= \
  NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
  /usr/bin/timeout 120s "$(command -v node)" --import tsx \
    scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts
```

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head=082f48e96 controlled local MS Teams SDK transport
entra-root: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>
client: starting real probeMSTeams() with redirected MSAL fetch
client: redirected body-stall https://login.microsoftonline.com/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
server: phase=body-stall POST /body-stall/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
client: phase=body-stall status=200 headers-sent
probe: bot elapsed=30002ms ok=false error=MS Teams Bot Framework probe token timed out after 30000ms
client: redirected normal-after https://login.microsoftonline.com/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
server: phase=normal-after POST /normal-after/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
client: phase=normal-after status=200 headers-sent
probe: graph elapsed=17ms ok=false error=Invalid token specified: missing part #2
probe: total elapsed=30524ms
assertion: graph bounded within 35s = true
assertion: bot bounded within 35s = true
proof: server closed cleanly
shellExit=0
```

Observation:
- The real `@azure/msal-node` POSTed the Bot Framework token request to the redirected loopback server (the body-stall phase).
- The body-stall server sent headers, then never called `res.end()`. MSAL's reader waited on the body.
- The production `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` wrapper aborted the SDK call at the 30-second production default (`probe: bot elapsed=30002ms`, error matches the documented `withTimeout` format: `"<label> timed out after <ms>ms"`).
- The graph call attempt immediately after completed in 17ms against the normal-after phase (the fake JWT in the response intentionally has no second segment so MSAL rejects the parse — proves the second call is not poisoned by the first's abort and the wrapper's deadline doesn't leak across calls).
- Total wall-clock: 30.5s. Without the fix, the bot call would have hung indefinitely past the harness budget.
- The harness file (`scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts`) was deleted after the run; only the redacted transcript above survives in this PR body.

Known limits: this is controlled local SDK transport proof, not live Entra. The proxy env vars are set defensively in case the SDK spawns any other fetch (it did not in this run); MSAL constructs the token URL directly. Not tested: live Azure AD endpoint behavior, real Entra TLS, real MSAL production configuration, regional auth clouds, federated identity flow, managed identity flow.

### 4.3 What I checked

- **Current-main behavior**: stock-pinned `a788617325` (main) still has naked `await tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89`; a never-settling promise leaves the probe pending indefinitely.
- **Proposed runtime repair**: PR head routes both token acquisitions through the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` helper from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`, preserving the existing outer catch at `:138` and the graph-specific inner catch at `:110`.
- **Existing owner pattern**: the same `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` helper is already in use at 8 sibling MS Teams sites (see the table in section 4.5). The probe was the one missing consumer; this PR brings it in line with the established pattern.
- **Test cost reduction**: the original committed test waited 90 seconds of wall-clock per focused run (3 stalled cases × 30s deadline); the rewrite uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` to drive the same `withTimeout` race in milliseconds, with one extra case asserting the production default is `30_000`.
- **P1 proof**: the `scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts` harness (deleted after the run) drove the production `probeMSTeams` entry point through the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` App + real `@azure/msal-node` against a stalled loopback server. The transcript above shows the bounded 30-second abort and the recovery on the subsequent graph call.
- **Automated validation**: the existing GitHub context (lint, prod types, test types, extension-boundary checks, Node test shards, security-fast, Opengrep, real-behavior-proof workflow) all pass on the PR head; these supplement but do not replace the contributor proof.

### 4.4 Regression coverage

The committed [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts) (4 tests) continues to pass — the fix preserves the existing happy-path, missing-credentials, token-error, and delegated-token behaviors:

```
 ✓  returns an error when credentials are missing                          3ms
 ✓  validates credentials by acquiring a token                              2ms
 ✓  returns a helpful error when token acquisition fails                    1ms
 ✓  reports delegated tokens expired when the process clock is invalid      2ms
```

### 4.5 Impact-surface review

`probeMSTeams` is the only consumer of `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` in `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts`. Every other MS Teams path that calls `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` is already wrapped in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`:

| File:line | Label | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `attachments/bot-framework.ts:252` | `MS Teams Bot Framework token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `attachments/graph.ts:258` | `MS Teams Graph media token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:594` | `Teams media list` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:654` | `Teams graph token (for quote)` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:685` | `Teams graph token (for download)` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:692` | `Teams parent + replies` | ✓ wrapped |
| `attachments/download.ts:167` | `Teams attachment token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `team-identity.ts:37` | `Team identity lookup` | ✓ wrapped |
| **`probe.ts:75` (this PR)** | `MS Teams Bot Framework probe token` | **fixed** |
| **`probe.ts:89` (this PR)** | `MS Teams Graph probe token` | **fixed** |

The probe was the one missing site. No new helper, no new public API, no SDK change.

### 4.6 Sibling reference

This PR is part of the same network-layer "additive defense" wave:

- [#106034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106034) `fix(google): bound realtime browser token requests` — Alix-007, MERGED 2026-07-13 — closest analog for the scratchpad proof shape (controlled local SDK transport via a temporary uncommitted harness with a real `node:http` server). target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(message): preserve stringified channelData payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where message actions that pass channel-specific `channelData` as a JSON string could lose that payload or fail to treat it as send content when the visible text is blank or removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message tool, outbound runner, and embedded subscribe rich-content tracker now parse `channelData` with the same structured JSON boundary used for sibling message payload fields. The shared structured-content helpers keep oversized legacy files from growing while preserving the same dispatch behavior. The message-tool path also rejects opaque `channelData` that contains protected internal runtime context before dispatch, and the runner now counts valid object-shaped `channelData` as real send content without adding config, schema, provider, or compatibility behavior.

Duplicate search found no open or closed overlapping PRs or open issues for `channelData JSON message action`, `stringified channelData`, `message-tool channelData idempotency`, or `parseJsonMessageParam channelData`; open self PRs had no same-root outbound/message parameter normalization overlap.

## User Impact

Channel-native cards, buttons, and other provider payload metadata can be preserved when passed as JSON strings, including internal source replies that intentionally carry channel-specific structured data without visible text. Protected runtime context remains filtered before those opaque payloads can be sent.

## Evidence
### Real internal-source proof (exact head 641c0c0fe8c4e302a92d0c1d25d236b62cbf9291)

Command:

``powershell
@' <script omitted: calls createMessageTool({ currentChannelProvider: "webchat", sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only" }).execute(...) without injecting runMessageAction and without dryRun> '@ | node --import tsx --input-type=module -
``

Observed redacted terminal output:

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw parses `openclaw.json` using JSON5, which supports comments. However, when the configuration is modified, the system saves back using standard `JSON.stringify()`, which strips all user-authored comments.

**Issue**: #105683

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `src/config/io.ts` where config writes use `JSON.stringify()` which cannot preserve JSON5 comments.

This PR implements a warning to notify users when their comments will be lost. The warning is **not** gated on `skipOutputLogs` — comment stripping is a data-loss event that should always be surfaced, even for machine-parseable (`--json`) callers.

## User Impact

### Before
- Users add comments to `openclaw.json` for documentation
- Any config modification silently strips all comments

### After  
- Users receive a clear warning when writing config with JSON5 comments
- The warning fires regardless of output mode (including `--json` / `skipOutputLogs`)
- The warning intelligently excludes false positives (URLs in strings)

## Evidence

### Runtime Proof — Real Config Mutation

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  BEFORE — config file with JSON5 comments:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
{
  // Gateway configuration — selects local mode for development
  "gateway": {
    "mode": "local" // runs the gateway on the local machine
  },
  /* Plugin block:
     add extension plugin entries below */
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {}
  },
  /**
   * Multi-line doc-comment style block
   * describing the agents section.
   */
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "main", "default": true }
    ]
  }
}

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  Writing config via createConfigIO.writeConfigFile()...
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  ⚠️  WARN: Config write will strip JSON5 comments from
  /tmp/.../openclaw.json. Use a separate tool to re-add
  documentation comments after modifications.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  AFTER — config file written by JSON.stringify:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
{
  "gateway": { "mode": "local" },
  "plugins": { "entries": {} },
  "agents": {
    "list": [{ "id": "main", "default": true }]
  },
  "meta": {
    "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.6.10",
    "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-13T07:07:04.780Z"
  }
}

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  VERIFICATION:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  Warning emitted:     ✅ PASS
  Comments stripped:   ✅ PASS

  ✅ PROOF SUCCESSFUL
```

### Implementation

1. **New `hasJSON5Comments()` function** (`src/config/io.ts`):
   - Deterministic single-pass character scanner detecting `//` and `/*` outside string literals
   - Handles JSON5 escape sequences, line continuations, and all quote styles
   - Avoids false positives on URLs (`http://`) and string content

2. **Warning logic**:
   - Fires on every config write when the original has JSON5 comments
   - NOT gated on `skipOutputLogs` — always surfaced since comment loss is data loss
   - Provides actionable guidance to users

3. **Comprehensive tests** (`src/config/io.write-config.test.ts`):
   - 10 tests covering line/block comments, inline comments, string-literal escapes, adversarial payloads, URL false-positives, `skipOutputLogs` bypass, rejected-write suppression, `$include` file detection, and escape-heavy backtracking benchmark

### Code Quality

- TypeScript compliant (no `any` types)
- Format check passes
- Follows existing patterns

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race. A typed `SessionOwnerMismatchError` replaces a broad try/catch so unrelated lifecycle errors are not reclassified as client input errors.
- **Files changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, `src/gateway/session-plugin-ownership.ts` (new), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (+271)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Feature / Refactor / Docs / Chore

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Auth / tokens / API / contracts / UI / CI

## Evidence

### Behavior

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` now enforces exact `pluginOwnerId` equality for plugin-runtime callers across 15 authenticated scenarios:

Cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Cross-plugin parent link — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent fork — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent link — rejected ✓
Cross-store cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Non-plugin client fork — allowed ✓
Self-owned parent — allowed, ownership propagated ✓
Existing-target takeover — rejected ✓
Parentless create — ownership stamped ✓

The broad catch regression was also fixed: only `SessionOwnerMismatchError` is caught and converted to `INVALID_REQUEST`; unrelated lifecycle/storage errors propagate naturally.

### Test results

```
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "assertCurrent|rejects cross-plugin|rejects cross-store"
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Full gateway test suite: 349/352 passed (3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change: node binding, hook mock, worktree git version).

target.title: fix(envelope): accept timestamp 0 in formatEnvelopeTimestamp
target.body:
## Summary

`formatEnvelopeTimestamp` used `if (!ts)` to check for missing timestamps, which incorrectly rejected the valid numeric timestamp `0` (Unix epoch). Replace the falsy check with an explicit `ts === undefined || ts === null` check.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/auto-reply/envelope.ts:117`, `formatEnvelopeTimestamp` guards with `if (!ts) { return undefined; }`. Since `ts` is typed `number | Date | undefined`, the value `0` is a valid millisecond timestamp (representing 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z), but `!0 === true` causes it to be silently rejected.

**Code evidence**: In `envelope.ts:117`, `!ts` is falsy for `0` (valid Unix epoch timestamp).

## Root Cause

The check `!ts` conflates "missing/undefined" with "falsy numeric value". For a parameter typed `number | Date | undefined`, the only invalid value is `undefined` (and technically `null`). Using `!` also rejects `0`, which is a valid timestamp.

## Why This Fix

The minimal fix: change `if (!ts)` → `if (ts === undefined || ts === null)`. This preserves the existing behavior for `undefined` and `Date` instances (always truthy) while correctly accepting `0`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0)` silently returns `undefined` — the Unix epoch timestamp is dropped from envelope formatting.
- **After**: `formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0)` returns `"Thu 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"` (in UTC mode).

## Evidence

- **Before**: `formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0)` returns `undefined` → FAIL
- **After**: `formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0)` returns formatted timestamp → PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
=== formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0) ===
FAIL: formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0) returned undefined
      The valid Unix epoch timestamp is being rejected by the falsy check.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
=== formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0) ===
Result: Thu 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
PASS: formatEnvelopeTimestamp(0) correctly formatted the Unix epoch timestamp.

=== formatEnvelopeTimestamp(undefined) ===
Result: undefined
PASS: undefined correctly returns undefined.
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 2 regression tests: timestamp 0 is formatted; undefined still returns undefined

target.title: fix(restart-sentinel): log DB errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## Summary

`clearRestartSentinel`, `readRestartSentinel`, and `hasRestartSentinel` used empty `catch {}` / `catch { return null }` / `catch { return false }` blocks that silently swallowed SQLite DB errors. This PR replaces them with `sentinelLog.warn(...)` so errors are visible in diagnostics while preserving the best-effort semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, three exported functions silently discard all errors from the SQLite state database:

- **`clearRestartSentinel`** — `catch {}`: If the DB write fails (locked, corrupt, disk full), the sentinel is not cleared but the caller has no way to detect this. The gateway may continue to believe a restart is pending.
- **`readRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return null }`: Any DB read error (transient lock, corruption) is treated identically to "no sentinel exists", potentially causing a pending restart to be silently dropped.
- **`hasRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return false }`: Same problem — DB errors are indistinguishable from "no sentinel".

**Code evidence**: In `restart-sentinel.ts:228`, the `catch {}` on the `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` call provides no visibility into whether the sentinel was actually cleared.

## Root Cause

The functions were written with best-effort semantics (they must not throw during shutdown/cleanup), but the empty catch blocks went too far by discarding all diagnostic information. Unlike the intentional best-effort pattern in `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` (which includes a comment explaining why the catch is empty), these catch blocks had no explanation and no logging.

## Why This Fix

Follows the same pattern accepted in:
- [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) (`fix(delivery): log failDelivery errors instead of silently swallowing`) by @SebTardif
- [#82943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82943) (`fix(agents): log warnings instead of swallowing subagent errors`) by @SebTardif

Uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart-sentinel")` + `formatErrorMessage(err)` — consistent with `restart.ts` which also uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart")`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Operators had no diagnostic signal when the restart sentinel could not be cleared or read — failures were completely invisible.
- **After**: A warning is emitted to the diagnostics log (`[restart-sentinel]` prefix) with the full error context, while the functions continue to return safe defaults (`null` / `false` / `undefined`).

## Evidence

- **Before**: No warnings emitted on stderr when the DB operation fails — errors are silently swallowed.
- **After**: Three warnings emitted with full error context; functions return safely without throwing.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, `catch {}`)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
      The catch blocks are silently swallowing errors.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
PASS: Warnings were emitted on stderr:
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to clear restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to read restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to check restart sentinel: ...
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 3 regression tests in `restart-sentinel.test.ts` verifying that each function survives DB failures without throwing and returns the safe default value

target.title: fix(feishu): pass timeoutMs through app-registration guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: exported `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts`
- Production caller path: `beginAppRegistration` → `postRegistration` → `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`
- Regression: `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts`
- ClawSweeper follow-up: non-Vitest standalone runtime proof of the production guarded-fetch call shape, including the full 10s default floor

Closes #103668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running bash commands through agents could see ANSI/OSC control-sequence fragments leak into streamed tool output, final bash results, and full-output spill files when a process split a terminal sequence across output callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a reusable incremental ANSI sequence stripper in terminal-core and lets the bash output accumulator use one sanitizer instance for the lifetime of each command. This preserves streaming and bounded-memory behavior while keeping one-shot `stripAnsiSequences()` semantics unchanged for existing callers.

## User Impact

Bash output sanitization is now invariant to callback chunking for OSC and CSI sequences. Agents and users receive the same clean output whether the process emits a complete sequence in one callback or splits it across callbacks.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: exported `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

target.title: fix(cli-backends): surface config-defined custom CLI backends in runtime model bindings (fixes #106373)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `sessions.compact` throws `MissingAgentHarnessError` for sessions running on a config-defined custom CLI backend — a backend declared only under `agents.defaults.cliBackends`, not owned by any plugin. Execution of the same session works correctly because `resolveCliBackendConfig` recognizes config-only backends, but the compaction and harness-selection paths do not, because `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` only consults the plugin runtime registry and optional setup registry — never the user's `agents.defaults.cliBackends` config.

Concrete example: defining a second Claude Code account (`claude-cli-max`) with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under `cliBackends` works for agent turns, but every `sessions.compact` request against that session fails with `MissingAgentHarnessError: Requested agent harness "claude-cli-max" is not registered.`

## Why This Change Was Made

`listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` now also surfaces config-defined custom CLI backends that resolve to a valid config (non-null `resolveCliBackendConfig`). This aligns it with the existing `isCliProvider` function in `model-selection-cli.ts`, which already recognizes config-only backends. The asymmetry — `isCliProvider` sees the backend but `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` and its callers (`isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`, `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider`) do not — caused the compaction and harness precheck paths to miss config-only backends while the execution path handled them.

Two additional pass-through fixes: `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` and `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider` now forward `config`/`env` to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` instead of calling it without parameters. A single call site in `harness/selection.ts` now forwards `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (the other call site in the same file already did).

Backends already in the plugin registry are never duplicated; backends without a valid `command` are silently omitted.

## User Impact

Users with config-defined custom CLI backends (e.g. multiple Claude Code accounts, or any non-plugin CLI runtime) can now run `sessions.compact` without `MissingAgentHarnessError`. Agent execution, harness selection, and compaction preflight all treat these backends consistently.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/cli-backends.ts` — the three-line core change adding config-only backends to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings`, plus two config-forwarding fixes.
- `src/agents/harness/selection.ts` — one-line forwarding of `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — six new cases covering: inclusion of a valid config-only backend, resolution via `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` returning true, omission when no config is passed or the backend lacks a command, and non-duplication of plugin-registered backends with config-level overrides.
- Full test run: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — 64 passed; `pnpm test src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.test.ts src/agents/model-selection-cli.test.ts` — 25 passed. No regressions.

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts -t "config-defined backends"

 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > includes a config-only custom CLI backend with a valid command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > resolves a binding for a config-only backend via resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider returns true for a config-only backend
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend when no config is passed
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend with no command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > does not duplicate a plugin-registered backend with a config-level override

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The six tests exercise `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` (before — no config → custom backend absent), `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` (after — with config → custom backend bound), and `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (after — returns true), covering all three patched functions plus the edge cases.

target.body:
# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

```text

```

Focused behavior:

```bash

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to

- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider

- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

@clawsweeper review

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root-work set to the direct-stop path. The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll (not `.unref()`) so the timer keeps the event loop alive. Bounded at 2 seconds; the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after return. Per ClawSweeper clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at `run-loop.ts:705` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710; the drain is self-bounded by its own referenced timer.

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Pending `session_end` hooks get up to 2 seconds to complete before exit. Stuck hooks cannot block shutdown.

#### Evidence

**1. Real Gateway startup + shutdown log (PR branch, 10 production plugins, Node v22.23.1)**

```
[gateway] loading configuration…

## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). ## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/clawhub.ts` uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` to parse the Content-Length response header — the same pattern that was replaced in `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` by #105954. target.title: fix(telegram): Mini App hangs on Opening dashboard when auth never responds
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram Mini App dashboard bootstrap could hang forever on **"Opening dashboard..."** when the same-origin `auth` fetch never returned (stalled upstream / hung TCP). The generated page had no request deadline, so `.catch(showExpired)` never ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the Mini App-owned `auth` fetch with a **15s** hang floor using an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` (not `AbortSignal.timeout`), so older Telegram WebViews that lack the static timeout API still open the dashboard and still recover into the existing expired/retry status.

- Healthy auth clears the timer after settle (no late abort race)
- Stalled auth aborts and hits the existing `.catch(showExpired)` path
- No new config/env surface; auth validation / token minting unchanged

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung Mini App `auth` request left the WebView on “Opening dashboard...” indefinitely.

**After:** After 15s the page shows “This link expired. Reopen the dashboard from your bot chat.” so the user can retry from the bot chat. Clients without `AbortSignal.timeout` are not broken by a synchronous throw before `fetch`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.ts`
- Regressions: `page.test.ts`, `page.auth-timeout.test.ts`, `routes.test.ts`

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.auth-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.test.ts --reporter=verbose

target.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
target.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` (or with `--agent` on the parent `models` command) would silently read and write the global `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain instead of the named agent's own fallback chain. `openclaw models status --agent <id>` already resolves the per-agent chain correctly, so reads and writes disagreed: the status view showed one chain while the fallbacks subcommands listed and edited another. The `image-fallbacks` group silently ignored `--agent` too.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `models fallbacks` subcommands now thread `--agent` the same way `models status` does (via `resolveModelAgentOption`), validate the id with the same `resolveKnownAgentId` guard `models status` uses (unknown ids error instead of silently editing global defaults), read the agent's own fallbacks override when it has one, and write through a new `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks` helper that mirrors the existing `setAgentEffectiveModelPrimary` pattern (mutate the agent's `agents.list[]` entry when it owns an override, otherwise update `agents.defaults.model`). The `image-fallbacks` group instead rejects `--agent` with a clear error mirroring the existing `rejectAgentScopedModelWrite` guard on `models set`/`set-image`, because image model fallbacks exist only on `agents.defaults.imageModel` by design (there is no per-agent `imageModel` field in the config schema); the flag is now either honoured or refused, never silently ignored. The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) stays global in all cases; only the fallback list itself is agent-scoped.

## User Impact

Operators of multi-agent deployments can now inspect and edit a single agent's fallback chain from the CLI: `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` operates on that agent's chain when the agent has its own model override, and on the global defaults otherwise (matching what `models status --agent <id>` reports). Without `--agent`, behaviour is unchanged. `models image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` now fails fast with an explanatory message instead of silently editing global defaults.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` cover `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks`: agent-override writes go to the agent entry (defaults untouched), no-override writes go to defaults, clearing in place, and an agent with an explicit primary but no fallbacks yet.
- New CLI wiring tests in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` cover `--agent` forwarding for fallbacks list/add/remove/clear (parent and subcommand flag placement), the unchanged no-agent path, rejection of parent `--agent` for all four `image-fallbacks` subcommands, and the unchanged no-agent image path.
- New e2e tests in `src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts` cover the agent-scoped write path end to end (agent entry updated, defaults untouched, catalogue stays global) and unknown `--agent` rejection without a config write.
- `docs/cli/models.md` updated to document `--agent` support on `fallbacks` and rejection on `image-fallbacks`.

target.title: fix(transcript-stream): log stat/open errors instead of silently returning empty iterator
target.body:
## Summary

`streamSessionTranscriptLines` and `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` used bare `catch { return; }` blocks that silently swallowed all filesystem errors. Replace them with `catch (err) { transcriptLog.warn(...); return; }`.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/config/sessions/transcript-stream.ts`, both streaming functions catch `fs.promises.stat` / `fs.promises.open` errors and silently return empty iterators. While an empty iterator is the correct contract for missing files, other errors (permission denied, I/O error) should be visible in diagnostics.

## Root Cause

The functions were designed to return an empty iterator when the file cannot be read, but the empty catch blocks discarded all diagnostic information.

## Why This Fix

Same pattern as [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) and [#106385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106385) — `createSubsystemLogger` + `formatErrorMessage(err)`.

## Evidence

- **Before**: EACCES error silently swallowed → empty iterator, no diagnostic
- **After**: EACCES error logged → `[transcript-stream] Failed to stat transcript /root/nonexistent-transcript.jsonl: EACCES: permission denied`

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
Lines collected: 0
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
Lines collected: 0
PASS: Warning was emitted on stderr:
  [transcript-stream] Failed to stat transcript /root/...: EACCES: permission denied
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed
- Added regression test for permission error path

target.body:
## Summary

fix(agents): tighten count-like schema fields to Type.Integer across built-in tools

**Problem**: Four built-in tool schemas use `Type.Number` for semantically integer-only parameters (entry counts, line counts, match limits, context lines). Fractional values like `10.5` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change all count-like fields to `Type.Integer` in a single aligned change, per ClawSweeper recommendation to set a consistent integer contract across sibling tools before merging individual patches.

**What changed**: `ls.ts` -> `lsSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `read.ts` -> `readSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `find.ts` -> `findSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `grep.ts` -> `grepSchema.limit: Type.Integer` and `grepSchema.context: Type.Integer`. All five schemas exported for production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: `bash.ts` `timeout` stays `Type.Number` — fractional seconds are meaningful for timeouts.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Count-like tool parameters now reject fractional values at schema-validation time before tool logic runs.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw main@5fe6ad9830a (HEAD of this PR).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx verify-schemas.ts` imports actual production schemas from ls.js/read.js/find.js/grep.js and calls TypeBox Value.Check() with integer and fractional inputs for each changed field.

**After-fix evidence**: Exact-head terminal transcript below validates all five fields against the real registered production schemas at this PR's HEAD (5fe6ad9830a), not a reconstructed copy. Both integer acceptance and float rejection confirmed per field.
```
=== Production schema integer validation (exact HEAD) ===
Testing that all five changed fields reject floats via real registered schemas.

  PASS  lsSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  readSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  findSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  grepSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  grepSchema.context
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)

Result: ALL PASS ✓
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All five count-like schema fields reject fractional values while accepting valid integers at the schema-validation boundary.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool invocation with fractional values. The same TypeBox Check() runs at the tool-call parsing boundary so rejection would also happen there, but this is not demonstrated.

## merge-risk

🚨 This change may break existing users, config, or upgrade paths — tools that currently accept and silently floor/truncate fractional values will now reject them at schema level. The risk is limited to callers passing non-integer count arguments, which are semantically nonsensical and unlikely in practice.

- Single clean commit per convention

- [x] All existing tests pass

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render with grapheme-leading name:
  - Real Lit component renders with textContent = "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + Component test
- Target test files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji initial, joined emoji grapheme, flag grapheme, skin-tone grapheme, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path with surrogate pair preservation
  - Selector: grapheme cluster preserved in real Lit component DOM render
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact grapheme boundary at both helper and component level, plus browser compatibility path.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit) and later `codePointAt(0)` (first code point), neither of which respects grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No grapheme-aware initial derivation; agent selector had a separate inconsistent fallback; no Intl.Segmenter feature detection for browser compatibility.

target.title: fix(agents): reject aborted foreground exec with AbortError
target.body:
Closes #105681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where canceling a foreground `exec` tool call via the agent `AbortSignal` still fulfilled the tool result as a normal process exit/failure payload. The agent manager could treat the tool as completed instead of aborted, so cancellation did not cleanly surface as an abort error on the tool path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Foreground abort already kills the child process, but the wrapper promise still resolved through `buildExecForegroundResult` after the process exited. This change records caller abort for foreground runs, clears any armed yield timer before kill (so the timer cannot resolve a "running" result first), waits for the existing process finalization promise, then rejects with the signal reason or a canonical `AbortError`. Backgrounded/yielded sessions remain detached and are not killed by the tool-turn abort. Timeouts and ordinary non-abort process failures still use the existing normalized result path.

**Fix quality check:** compatibility — no config/API surface change; performance — O(1) flag/timer clear on abort only; usability — abort surfaces as `AbortError` instead of a misleading completed tool result; security — no trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

When an operator or agent runtime cancels a foreground bash/exec tool mid-run, the tool promise rejects with `AbortError` after process finalization instead of returning a successful-looking failed/exit tool payload. Backgrounded process sessions are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: **local macOS**.

Branch refreshed onto current `main` (`merge(main)` → `11f1b1eef` / `11f1b1eef2b71efd58281348bde2cee02c7180e9`; base `1b43d7144`).

- Behavior addressed: Caller abort of a foreground exec tool must reject with `AbortError` after process finalization, not fulfill a normal foreground result; yield timer must not win the race and resolve "running". Agent-loop path must not request another model turn after a tool abort.
- Environment: local macOS, Node v24.17.0, checkout `openclaw` at branch `fix/105681-exec-abort-reject` (`11f1b1eef` after merge with current main), real shell via production `createExecTool` (tsx driver) plus focused Vitest suites.

## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.
